title: Defense Transferability Probe: Testing Whether Single-Turn Defenses Hold Under Multi-Turn Attacks

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly addresses the 'adaptive defenses' open problem. If defenses break under multi-turn conditions, current deployment practices create a false sense of security. Clear chain from measurement to defense selection guidance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: AISafetyLab provides 16 defense mechanisms, reducing setup burden. But implementing multi-turn attack variants of single-turn attacks requires prompt engineering skill. Running 5-8 defenses x 2 conditions is feasible but time-intensive.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 5-8 defenses x 2 conditions (single vs multi-turn) x matched attack sets is a large experimental matrix. The 'defense transferability score' is a clear metric but computing it across all conditions is substantial. Limit to 4-5 defenses to fit 30 hours.
